items.headline: Blue Origin blames main oxygen valve on BE-4 engine for New Glenn pad explosion
items.title: Blue Origin identifies engine issue behind New Glenn explosion
items.scifi_hook: A faulty valve detonated a massive rocket on the launch pad, turning a future launch into a fiery spectacle.
items.eli5: The main oxygen valve in one of the rocket's engines failed, causing the whole New Glenn rocket to explode during a test.
items.why: Engine reliability is crucial for commercial heavy‑lift launch schedules and competition.
items.text: Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket exploded on the pad at Launch Complex 36 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station as the result of an anomaly during a static fire test on Thursday, May 28. The test was in preparation for a planned launch as soon as June 4. Image: Adam Bernstein/Spaceflight Now Correction Aug. 6, 8:52 p.m. EDT (0052 UTC): Fixed a line suggesting that Amazon Leo satellites were on the New Glenn rocket when it exploded. That was not the case. Blue Origin CEO Dave Limp said an issue with the main oxygen valve on a BE-4 engine was the source of the explosion that destroyed a New Glenn rocket during a static fire in May ahead of the company’s fourth orbital flight. “The anomaly originated at the main oxygen valve on one of the BE-4 engines, which was later confirmed by hardware recovery and inspections,” Limp wrote in a social media post that came more than two months after the blast that damaged Blue Origin’s sole orbital launch site, Launch Complex 36 at Cape Canaveral. “Extensive component-level and engine hotfire tests have been conducted to understand the failure mode better and inform mitigations.” ﻿ The New Glenn rocket is powered by a total of seven BE-4 engines on its first stage. They’re fueled by a combination of liquid methane and liquid oxygen and are each capable of producing 640,000 pounds of force at liftoff. items.headline: SpaceX Falcon 9 second stage crashes into Moon, creating sodium‑lithium plume
items.title: SpaceX rocket stage crashes into moon, scientists confirm
items.scifi_hook: A stray rocket stage slammed into the lunar surface, lighting up the Moon with a brief chemical fireworks show.
items.eli5: A leftover piece of a SpaceX rocket hit the Moon at high speed, releasing gases that telescopes detected.
items.why: Shows growing amount of space debris and need for tracking lunar environment.
items.text: A SpaceX rocket stage floating in space since last year smashed into the moon at high speed early Wednesday morning, joining the ranks of meteoroids, wayward spacecraft ​and other pieces of space junk that have bombarded the lunar surface for ages, astronomers confirmed. The school-bus-size object is the second stage of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket that launched a lunar lander from Firefly Aerospace toward the moon in January 2025. While the rocket's booster returned to Earth, the upper stage remained in space after completing its primary mission. The unintentional collision occurred at around 2:35 a.m. ET (0635 GMT), when the 4,000-kilogram rocket stage slammed into the moon at a speed of about 8,690 kilometers per hour. The impact had been predicted months in advance by astronomers tracking the object's trajectory. The crash posed no threat to Earth, and no spacecraft orbiting the moon were positioned to capture close-up images of the impact. But the European Southern Observatory's (ESO) Very Large Telescope in Chile detected glimmers of light associated with the impact. "We can confirm that the telescope detected spectral lines of sodium and lithium gas in the impact plume lasting for 5-10 minutes after impact," an ESO spokesperson told Reuters. NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter probe and South Korea's Pathfinder Lunar Orbiter were also expected to take images of the impact site, though it could take days to receive that information. items.headline: Blue Origin confirms BE-4 engine oxygen valve as cause of New Glenn accident
items.title: Blue Origin narrowing in on root cause of catastrophic rocket accident
items.scifi_hook: Investigators pinpoint a single valve failure as the spark that destroyed a next‑generation heavy‑lift rocket.
items.eli5: Blue Origin says the problem started at the main oxygen valve of one of its seven BE-4 engines during a hot‑fire test.
items.why: Understanding the failure guides future design fixes and impacts launch market confidence.
items.text: Blue Origin provided its first substantive update this week on the cause of the catastrophic loss of the New Glenn rocket and most of its launch pad infrastructure at Cape Canaveral, Florida, in May. The space company's chief executive, Dave Limp, said investigative work is continuing into the anomaly that happened during a hot-fire test of the rocket during the evening of May 28, 2026. He confirmed, for the first time, widespread speculation that the problem started in one of the rocket's seven BE-4 engines that power the vehicle's first stage. "The anomaly originated at the main oxygen valve on one of the BE-4 engines, which was later confirmed by hardware recovery and inspections," he said. "Extensive component-level and engine hotfire tests have been conducted to understand the failure mode better and inform mitigations." Read full article Comments

items.headline: Perpetua discovers tungsten potential at Idaho Stibnite project
items.title: Perpetua makes tungsten discovery at Gold-Stibnite project in Idaho
items.scifi_hook: A new source of ultra‑dense tungsten may revive U.S. production for aerospace and defense hardware.
items.eli5: Perpetua found signs of tungsten, a metal used in high‑performance tools and weapons, in its Idaho mining project.
items.why: Domestic tungsten could reduce reliance on China for a critical defense material.
items.text: Perpetua Resources (Nasdaq: PPTA) (TSX: PPTA) said on Thursday it has identified gold and antimony exploration targets with the potential for extensions of the permitted pits within its Stibnite project in Idaho, and that it identified potential sources of tungsten. Tungsten is a critical mineral that has the highest melting point of any metal, and extreme density, making it essential for heavy industry, aerospace engineering, advanced electronics, and military defense systems like armor-piercing ammunition. Tungsten production in the US ceased in 2015. The US had been mining tungsten, but it was no longer commercially viable due to low prices and competition from China. China dominates global tungsten production, accounting for over 80% of last year’s total output of 81,000 tons, according to the USGS. “Our focus is on drilling areas that align with our currently planned mining sequence with potential to directly add value,” Perpetua CEO Jon Cherry said in a news release. “Our priority is testing higher-grade gold and antimony targets within our three permitted pits that could supplement our existing Stibnite Gold project mine plan with the aim of sustaining or exceeding our estimated annual average production level of 463,000 gold ounces beyond our first four years of production.” How a gold-stibnite restoration in Idaho could add antimony to US supply chain The company said recent drilling between the currently permitted Yellow Pine and West End reserve pits continues to r

items.headline: JAIST uses Bayesian localization to sharpen neural‑network material simulations
items.title: JAIST’s Bayesian localization boosts accuracy of neural network simulations
items.scifi_hook: Japanese researchers fuse Bayesian math with AI to simulate materials faster than ever.
items.eli5: A new Bayesian method lets neural nets predict material properties with less computer power.
items.why: It cuts cost and time for designing new materials, speeding innovation.
items.text: JAIST researchers paired neural networks with a ‘Bayesian localization of pseudo Hamiltonian’ approach, reducing computational costs for accurate material property simulations.

items.why: Large funding accelerates development of practical quantum systems.
items.text: Rigetti Computing reported $5.1 million in Q2 2026 revenue, with $541.3 million to fund continued development of its full-stack quantum-classical computing systems.
